request.hypothesis: How do private-value LLM bidders behave in a sealed-bid second-price auction compared with truthful bidding?
requirements: This is an agent simulation, not a standalone optimization task. Use the existing policy, observation/privacy, protocol, mechanism, runtime and recording interfaces.
Actors are bidder_a, bidder_b and bidder_c in that configuration order. Each is an LLM policy using MODEL, not a scripted fixture. MODEL_CODING is only for the external coding agent.

One simultaneous sealed-bid round, one action per bidder. Bidders see the auction rules and only their own private valuation/memory, never another bidder's private state or submitted bid before committing.
Textbook independent private values with risk-neutral quasi-linear utility, one indivisible item, no reserve and no budget constraints. Record these assumptions in configuration.
A bid is a finite nonnegative number. Bidding above or below one's valuation is legal. Do not reject a bid merely because it is strategically poor or would produce negative utility.

Highest bid wins, pays the second-highest submitted bid, and has utility own valuation minus payment. Other bidders pay zero and have utility zero. Break highest-bid ties by the stated configuration order and record that convention.

Compute a separate truthful-bidding reference from private valuations after the LLM decisions are committed. Explain that truthfulness is weakly dominant under these assumptions; do not claim it is the unique equilibrium or label every nontruthful bid irrational.

Provide custom verification for allocation, payment, utilities, ties and bid legality. Do not force the piecewise auction rules into an unsuitable numeric expression language or invent irrelevant simplex/budget checks.

Generate an executed results notebook comparing actual bids with private valuations and the truthful reference, actual versus reference winners/payments/payoffs, and the recorded decision rationales and assumptions.
Use real LLM policies in the primary simulation. Execution capabilities are supplied separately; never replace requested live actors with scripted decisions.

The notebook must teach a reader without domain knowledge: explain the background and rationale, interpret the observed results and theoretical comparison, show recorded decision rationales once in their own section, list assumptions in ordinary prose/bullets, and explain limitations. Use the toolkit explanatory.v1 reporting contract.

A separately calculated theoretical point reference is sufficient; a new equilibrium solver is not a requirement. Keep all domain calculations outside notebook cells and derive report data from the saved run and resolved configuration.

policy_parameters.instructions: You are bidding in the sealed-bid second-price auction described in the visible 'rules'. Your private valuation appears in your private facts. Submit exactly one action of kind 'submit_bid' with payload {"bid": <your bid as a finite nonnegative number>}. Your bid may be above, below, or equal to your valuation. Base your decision only on information in your observation; do not invent other bidders' valuations or bids, and do not claim knowledge of choices that have not been revealed. Include a concise rationale that cites your valuation and explains your chosen bid.
policy_parameters.persona: You are bidder_a, one of three bidders (bidder_a, bidder_b, bidder_c) competing for one indivisible item.

initial_public_state.rules: Sealed-bid second-price auction for one indivisible item. Each bidder privately knows only their own valuation and submits exactly one sealed bid, a finite nonnegative number. Bids are revealed only after every bidder has committed. The highest bid wins; the winner pays the second-highest submitted bid. The winner's payoff equals their own valuation minus the price paid; every other bidder pays nothing and receives zero. Ties for the highest bid are broken by bidder order: bidder_a first, then bidder_b, then bidder_c. There is no reserve price and no budget constraints. Bidding above or below your own valuation is allowed.

assumptions.rationale: The user requires highest-bid ties to be broken by configuration order (bidder_a, then bidder_b, then bidder_c).
The user requires one simultaneous sealed-bid round with one action per bidder.

The settlement implements the textbook second-price sealed-bid (Vickrey) rules under independent private values with risk-neutral quasi-linear utility: the highest bid wins and pays the second-highest submitted bid, the winner's utility is valuation minus payment, and losers receive zero.
